Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

absence noun

also in my absence, in your absence, while I was away, while you were away

classical

Traupman 92, 267: mē absente
Cic. Fam. 3.11.2: tē absentem

mē absente

ablative absolute of absēns, absentis, participle of absum

in my absence, while I am (was) away

Latin speaks of the absent person, not of an abstract absence: tē absente, in your absence; absentī mihi, to me while I was away.

Other words

  • absentia, absentiae f. — absence, being away

    noun, first declension · also used · classical · Cic. Pis. 37: cōnfer absentiam tuam cum meā (Lewis & Short) · Declension on Wiktionary

    Classical but much rarer than the participle. Quintilian also uses it for the lack of something (absentia testimōniōrum, Quint. 5.7.1); for that sense see lack.

Examples

  • complexus igitur sum cōgitātiōne tē absentem, epistulam vērō ōsculātus

    so I embraced you in my thoughts in your absence, and kissed the letterCic. Fam. 3.11.2

  • ut certiōrēs facerēmus absentīs, sī quid esset quod eōs scīre aut nostrā aut ipsōrum interesset

    to let those who are away know of anything that it matters to us or to them that they should knowCic. Fam. 2.4.1

  • cōnfer absentiam tuam cum meā

    compare your absence with mineCic. Pis. 37 (Lewis & Short)

  • Quid mē absente factum est?

    What happened while I was away?composed

See also away, presence, lack.
